name: 2100 Prairie Avenue — John B. Sherman house (Burnham & Root, 1874)

grade.why: Pictured: 3 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: Built 1874 (the marker) and drawn by the 1911 sheet; the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and the undated photograph (the library dates it c. 1885-1895) shows the house as this record builds it. This phase claims the 1904 target and the sheet's date, no more; the 1911 sheet's college lettering is a later use, not drawn.

placement.position_note: The rear south corner of the main body, 1.2 m south of the district draft's (which stood at lot frame u 21.000, v -2.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line): the body is widened to the traced outline's 14.2 m on the south (see the footprint). through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation -0.614 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 2100 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2100 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: The main body off the 1911 sheet's traced main part (s35fp-2100-b1 p1): 26.25 m from the rear to the parlour's front, the district draft's depth, and 14.2 m along Prairie Avenue, the traced outline's width between its flank lines (local n -3617.4 to -3631.6) where the draft took its largest inscribed rectangle, 13.0 m. The extra 1.2 m is laid on the south: the photograph, through its solved camera, put the porch and the corner where the draft stood and the library pavilion about 2-3 m south of where the draft's front would carry it. The plate's 1876 plan agrees in proportion (the library pavilion stands before this line as a bay). The sheet's small frame piece on the south flank (the plan's veranda) is not built.

stories.note: '3S.B.' on the 1911 sheet: the photograph and the 1876 plate both show two full storeys over a high basement under a slated mansard whose dormered attic is the sheet's third storey.

construction.note: The sheet colours the house brick; the photograph shows dark pressed brick between pale stone bands, a stone basement and stone dressings on every opening (the register's 'pressed dark-red brick with contrasting sandstone bands').

stone_front.note: The photograph shows smooth pale stone up to the principal floor's sill, under the dark brick of the storeys, on the front and the 21st Street flank alike; the register reads it as sandstone (the print is monochrome: K01's fawn sandstone is the kit's colour for it, liberty L-k01-2100-sherman-1919). T-3699: the brick between is banded in the same pale stone, three bands read off the photograph through its solved camera (data/reference_views/sherman_house_2100_prairie/chicagology_photo.json) on the parlour's bay (x 700-800 px): the stone runs on over the principal floor to the principal lights' sills (y 1270-1350 px, the panels under the lights in it), laid as belts from the basement's top to the sills (2.3 m); a deep band from the principal lights' heads to the second-storey sills (y 905-1060 px, about 5.8-7.8 m through the camera; the arches over the principal lights and the balcony's string course stand in it), laid from the heads (5.6 m) to the sills (7.7 m); and the frieze under the cornice (y 650-710 px), which is wall_head's frieze, over the dark brick band the photograph draws just above the second-storey heads (y 710-730 px). Each band is laid in courses of of 0.35 m or less (K01 lays none deeper than 0.40 m)'s deepest belt, so the joints between them are the kit's, not read.

side_base.note: The stone basement runs round the 21st Street flank in the photograph (K01's north wall); the south flank's is carried round the same way, which no picture shows (liberty L-k01-2100-sherman-1919).

principal_floor_m.note: The stoop's landing stands about 140-170 px over the walk at the fence's foot. The photograph is read at about 76 px a metre on the porch's plane (the woman standing on the stoop's landing, x 600-650 px, y 1235-1360, taken as 1.65 m), heights from the landing (y 1360) and the walk at the fence's foot (y 1530).

storey_heights_m.note: The balcony's floor over the porch (y 893 px at the porch's face) is about the second floor and the cornice's foot (y 640 px at the front) closes the second storey. The woman on the landing (x 600-650 px, y 1235-1360, taken as 1.65 m)) first gave 4.9 and 4.4 m, which the record rendered through the solved camera (data/reference_views/sherman_house_2100_prairie/chicagology_photo.json) printed about 100 px low at both lines, so both storeys are raised to meet them; she stands back on the landing and may be shorter than taken.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-2100-sherman-1919): the kit's front wall for a three-storey brick house.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-2100-sherman-1919): a corner house's flank is a street wall, so it is laid thicker than a party wall.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-2100-sherman-1919): the kit's common brick for the rear wall, which no picture shows.

face_brick.note: The photograph shows the same dark close-jointed pressed brick on the front and the 21st Street flank, so it is carried all round (the register's 'pressed dark-red brick with tight dark joints'); the print is monochrome, so the colour is the kit's.

roof_form.note: Both pictures show a steep slated roof rising from the cornice on every face they see, broken by dormers and stopped by a crested deck: a mansard on K05's steep lower faces.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-2100-sherman-1919): the deck over the mansard's curb, unseen from the street.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's blocks stand out about a third of a metre from the brick in the photograph (x 545-900 px along the front at y 600-660).

mansard.note: The photograph: the slated faces rise from the cornice (y 600 px) to the crested curb (y 300-380, about 3.6 m) at about 76 degrees; on the front a small dormer over the entrance (x 445-585) and a larger stone dormer with a roundel in its gable over the parlour (x 670-850); on the 21st Street face two tall gabled stone dormers behind the great stack (x 1170-1255 and 1290-1380), the plate showing the same pair. T-3702: the small dormer over the entrance is the photograph's stone face under a projecting stone shelf (its cornice, crop y 430 px at x 445-585), its light about 0.7 m across (38 px on the front's foreshortened plane at about 77 px a metre), and over the shelf a slated hood about 1.1 m high (y 345-430) leaning back into the mansard, K01's `hood` head; the large dormer over the parlour keeps its 55 degree gable and takes the photograph's stone coping up both rakes, the short engaged pinnacle with its spike at each shoulder (y 365) and the finial at its apex (y 220-240), K01's dormer ornament. The roundel in the large dormer's gable (y 290-330) is not built: K01's lower-face dormer has no roundel, and the match record keeps it open.

roof_covering.note: The photograph's lower faces are laid in small slates in even courses (the register's 'steep slate roof'); the deck is unseen and takes the kit's tin.

wall_head.note: A deep stone cornice, pale like the bands, runs along the front and the 21st Street flank at y 600-660 px; K10's moulded stone cornice, carried round the south flank too, which no picture shows. T-3699: under it the photograph draws a pale stone frieze over the second-storey heads (y 650-710 px) and a row of stone blocks carrying the cornice's corona, standing about 1.0 m apart along the front (x 540, 605, 670, 740, 805 and 870 px, 9.4-14.4 m along the front through the solved camera), each about 0.45 m tall: K10's blocks under the moulded cornice round a mansard (as 1815's and 1901's), at that spacing, and K10's frieze, 0.8 m deep, its foot about 0.3 m over the second-storey heads, where the photograph draws a dark brick band between the heads and the frieze. The blocks are evenly spaced where the photograph may pair them, and the dentil band under them is not laid: K10 builds neither on this cornice (see the match record).

street_front_trim.note: The kit's dressed surrounds on the front's lights (RECONSTRUCTED, L-k01-2100-sherman-1919), except where T-3699 reads the photograph: the parlour's principal light (x 720-810 px) is square-headed under a stone lintel with a carved segmental tympanum over it, its moulded arch springing at the head (y 1060 px) and rising about 0.5 m to its crown (y 1010 px, about 6.4 m through the solved camera), laid as K09's tympanum on a lintel (as 1827's), in the deep stone band; the second-storey light keeps K01's flat lintel, as the photograph draws a square stone head there.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The landing runs out under the porch to the columns (the plate's plan draws the stoop's flight from the porch's front edge).

stoop_width_m.note: The curved front flight in the photograph and the plan's flight. T-3718: 2.3 m on v 7.6, the photograph's width between its cheeks at the flight's head, between the south pier and the cluster's pedestal, where the 1876 plate's plan draws the flight from the library's corner to the three columns; a terrace at the landing's height either side carries the porch's pier and cluster on to the balcony's ends (`entrance_kit.terrace`).

entrance_bay.note: The hall's door in the middle of the front, between the library pavilion and the parlour (the plate's plan: vestibule, hall).

front_bays.note: The plan's front, read in proportion on the sheet's 14.2 m: the library behind the pavilion (its own lights are the pavilion's), the hall's door at v 7.5 and the parlour's one light a storey at v 11.1 (photograph x 720-810 px); the first entry stands behind the pavilion and carries no light the street sees.

sash_by_storey.note: The parlour's tall light (x 720-810 px, y 700-920 in the second storey, about 2.8 m) and the principal storey's lights to the floor's height. The photograph is read at about 76 px a metre on the porch's plane (the woman standing on the stoop's landing, x 600-650 px, y 1235-1360, taken as 1.65 m), heights from the landing (y 1360) and the walk at the fence's foot (y 1530).

basement_lights.note: The basement's lights under the 21st Street flank (x 1180-1300 px, y 1395-1510), each under a sloped stone hood that is T-1920's.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-2100-sherman-1919): the kit's two-over-two sash; the photograph's lights are mostly single panes, T-1920's to refine. T-3701: the light over the hall's door, opening onto the porch's balcony, is K06's French window (two casement leaves to the floor under a transom), the kit's own reconstruction of a balcony door (1816's, T-1886); the photograph shows its head and upper glass over the balcony's guard only.

side_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-2100-sherman-1919): the south flank faces the neighbour across a side yard and no picture shows it: four lights a storey at the kit's spacing, clear of the plan's veranda.

north_bays.note: The 21st Street flank (s from the front): three narrow lights a storey behind the corner (photograph x 1120-1300 px), the bay window of the plan's sitting room, and the rear part's lights, which only the plate's far end shows.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-2100-sherman-1919): the rear wall, which no picture shows.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the pavilion's two basement lights under its principal pair, low in the stone base as the 21st Street flank's are in the photograph (x 1180-1300 px); the pavilion's own are behind the fence and its scrolls
the library's tall pair under its stone arch in the photograph (x 60-215 px, y 750-940): about 3.2 m of light in a 5.4 m principal storey
the pavilion's second-storey pair in the photograph (x 55-200 px, y 540-660 behind the tree), about 2.6 m tall in a 5.0 m storey
the oriel's cheek lights in the photograph (x 910-935 px on its south cheek), narrow, about 2.3 m tall in a 4.6 m storey
the oriel's pair on its face to the corner in the photograph (x 965-1055 px, y 690-860, a colonnette between them), about 2.3 m tall in a 4.6 m storey
a canted bay's cheek light, narrower than an ordinary sash so it fits the cheek, as tall as the sitting room's front light
the sitting room's principal light, the full height of the principal storey's other lights (about 3.1 m in 5.4 m), as the plan's bay window

bays.note: Three projections. The LIBRARY PAVILION at the front's south end: the plan's library stands about 1.25 m before the parlour's face (built 0.8 m, K08's ceiling for a pavilion carried up past the eave) and about 5 m wide, its north cheek against the porch as the photograph shows it; the photograph carries it up through the cornice into a steep slated gable with a finial (apex at y 290 px, about 17 m through the solved camera), two tall lights a storey and one in the gable. The CORNER at the parlour's north-east angle: the plan's cut corner with the oriel's dashed square over it, and the photograph's oriel on the second storey (x 905-1100 px) under the steep slated pyramid with its finial (apex at y 100 px, about 20 m through the solved camera); T-3700: built as the photograph's and the plate's oriel, K08's turned square set across the corner on five stone corbel courses at the second floor (7.2 m), in stone, 1.55 m in radius so its face to the corner is about 2.2 m as the photograph's (x 935-1095 px), its storey 4.6 m so its cornice stands under the main cornice as the photograph's gable foot does; a narrow light on each cheek and the pair on its face (2.3 m, the photograph's y 690-860 px); under its face the plate's stone column, a shaft 0.36 m across with a base and a capital stopped under the corbels, on a pedestal from grade to the principal floor (the photograph's tree hides it; the plate draws it whole); over its face the small coped stone gable with its rose roundel (1.3 m high, the photograph's y 560-655 px); and behind the gable the slated pyramid springing from its eaves on the main cornice's line, flared at its foot (eave pitch 0.5 over its first 0.8 m) and steep above (4.2), its finial's foot at about y 130 px against the photograph's 130. The plan's cut corner is not made under it: the parlour's corner stands square behind the column (K01 lays no cut there; liberty L-k01-2100-sherman-1919). The SITTING ROOM's canted bay on the 21st Street flank, from the plan (3.4 m wide, 0.9 m out, about 11 m behind the front), one storey over the basement as the plan draws it; its height is reconstructed. T-3699: the library's tall pair (x 60-215 px) stands in moulded stone surrounds under one broad carved segmental tympanum spanning both lights (its crown at y 990 px), K09's tympanum with span_m over the pair; T-3702: the pavilion gable's carved panel (the photograph's pale carved field filling the apex over the gable's light, crop x 170-290, y 150-290 of the pavilion) is K08's gable panel with its leaf relief; the photograph's carving reads as a diaper lattice, a pattern K08 does not carve.

chimneys.note: The great stack on the 21st Street flank behind the corner (photograph x 1050-1145 px, its clustered flues' tops at y 185, about 19 m through the solved camera), which the plate also draws; the other two stacks are the plan's fireplaces on the south wall and the kitchen's, their heights the kit's. T-3702: the great stack's head off the photograph (crop at x 1020-1180, y 170-620 px): a dark brick shaft from a stone base, a stone head over corbel courses under a projecting cap (y 320-370), and on it a row of three round flue shafts with moulded tops about 1.9 m high (y 185-320, at about 70 px a metre at the stack), seen in a row running back from the street, so they stand in a row along the stack's long side (`across: x`). Built as the K15 carved Sherman stack (its corbel blocks under a corbelled head; its string bands and sunk panels omitted, the photograph's shaft showing neither) with the kit's slender 1.1 m `long` shaft on each flue, its cap at 17.9 m so the flues' tops stand at the photograph's 19.0 m: the kit has no 1.9 m flue shaft (adding one to the shared K15 kit would restale every house that reads it), so the head stands about 0.8 m higher than the photograph's and its shafts that much shorter. The two stacks the photograph does not see take the same head without shafts (RECONSTRUCTED, L-k01-2100-sherman-1919). The carved gablet on the head's street face is not built.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-2100-sherman-1919): the kit's copper; no downpipe shows on the front or the corner in the photograph.

entrance_kit.note: The porch before the hall: in the photograph stone piers and a cluster of three columns with carved capitals (x 525-595 px) carry a deep stone entablature and the second floor's balcony over it, railed by a carved stone balustrade (y 890-950 px, about 0.85 m); the plan draws the porch the hall's width before the vestibule. T-3701 read the porch off the photograph through the solved camera: the porch and its flight stand on the photograph's axis at v 8.0, 0.5 m north of the hall's door, 3.2 m wide (the door stays at v 7.5 under its south half, as the photograph's dark doorway stands left of the cluster), and the render's columns, cheeks and slab now print within about 40 px of the photograph's where they printed about 80 px south; the soffit is lowered to 5.8 m and the entablature deepened to 1.2 m, as the photograph's capitals stand about 0.6 m under the balcony's floor, so the deck stays at 7.15 m, the second floor's; the balcony's guard is raised to the photograph's 0.85 m, and the light over the door made a door onto the deck (`hood.door_over`, 1816's precedent, T-1886): the photograph's light over the porch runs down behind the guard, its foot hidden; the capitals are carved (the kit's two tiers of leaves under an abacus) and the south column stands on a 0.8 m pedestal; the flight's cheeks are swept from 0.6 m over the landing down to a block at the foot (the kit's highest head; the photograph's stand about 0.7-0.8 m over it), splayed out 0.35 m a side toward the walk as the plate's plan draws the flight widening at its foot, and the south cheek pierced by a row of four openings under its coping as the photograph's is (the plate draws both pierced; the photograph shows the north cheek's face carved with a roundel, not open). The north corner's column is the photograph's cluster (T-3717, K01's `columns.cluster`): three slender shafts about 0.24 m across, 0.15 m apart in a row along the front (read off the photograph through its solved camera: the render's shafts and gaps print in the photograph's proportion, about three to one), on one pedestal 1.15 m wide and 1.4 m over the landing, under one carved abacus; the photograph shows no more of the cluster than its front, so the row is laid along the front, which is inferred. T-3718 carried the porch north and south as the photograph and the plate's plan draw it: the balcony runs from the library pavilion's north face (v 5.75, its slab 0.05 m clear of the pavilion) to v 10.3, about 0.7 m further north and as far as the parlour's upper light beside it allows (`centre_v_m` 8.025, 4.55 m); its south end stands on a square stone pier 0.5 m on a side under a plain capital (`columns.pier`) where the photograph shows a plain pier at the pavilion's corner and the plan thickens the library's corner, and the cluster stands at v 9.4 (`columns.at_v_m`), inside the balcony's north end as the plan draws the three columns, so the balcony runs on past it as the photograph's does; the flight is narrowed to 2.3 m between the pier and the cluster (`stoop_v_m` 7.6), with a terrace either side at the landing's height under them, each behind a low pierced parapet (the kit's swept flight takes a terrace only so); and the balustrade is a stone band pierced with nine round openings, for the photograph's carved pierced panels. What stays otherwise than the pictures (the match record): the south pier's width, the cluster's place and the north end are read at the photograph's and the plan's scale; the balustrade's panels are round piercings, not carved; the terraces' parapets stand where the photograph's landing north of the cluster has an open rail; the north cheek's carved roundel is not built.

boundary.note: The photograph's low iron fence of scrolled panels on a stone curb between square stone piers with pyramidal caps, along the walk (y 1480-1545 px); K11's scroll band. The fence turning along 21st Street is not built: K11 lays no side-street iron yet (liberty L-k01-2100-sherman-1919).

yard.note: RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-2100-sherman-1919): the kit's yard: a flagged walk to the stoop. The house stood empty in 1904 after Sherman's death (the register); its upkeep is not read.

side_belts.note: T-3699: the front's three pale stone bands carried round the 21st Street flank (K01's north wall), where the photograph draws them at the same lines as the front (x 1100-1428 px: the stone to the principal sills at y 1260-1340, the deep band from the principal heads to the second-storey sills at y 970-1060, and the frieze over the second-storey heads, which is wall_head's), 0.03 m proud as the basement's side_base is, in courses of 0.35 m or less (K01's side belt). The south flank's are carried round the same way, which no picture shows (liberty L-k01-2100-sherman-1919).

function.note: The 1911 sheet labels the building with a 1911 use, '3S.B. brick building lettered McCORMICK MEDICAL COLLEGE, on the 21st Street corner', which the draft does not carry back to 1904 (the T-1837 register warns not to assume the 1904 use from it). The register's family row, 'Sherman Victorian Gothic', names it a house, so the 1904 function is inferred residence on that row and the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'John B. Sherman Residence. Built 1874'.

citations.citation: 'Residence of Mr. J. B. Sherman, Chicago.' Burnham & Root, architects. Heliotype plate with an inset 'Plan of First Story' (scale 1/16 inch to the foot). The American Architect and Building News, vol. I no. 40, 30 September 1876; James R. Osgood & Co., Boston.
what_it_supplies: the first storey's plan: rooms, the library's projection before the front, the hall's door, the parlour's cut corner and the oriel's square over it, the sitting room's canted bay on the flank, the veranda
the perspective's composition of the front and the 21st Street flank
what_it_does_not_supply: dimensions that hold at the plate's scale
the house as it stood in 1904

citations.citation: 2100 S. Prairie Avenue (John B. Sherman residence). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 2100 S. Prairie. A print of the same view is J. W. Taylor's, 'Sherman, John B., Residence', Art Institute of Chicago, Ryerson & Burnham Archives (mqc 29581).
what_it_supplies: the street front's composition: the library pavilion, the porch and balcony, the parlour and the corner oriel
the storeys: the high basement, the two storeys, the mansard's attic and the pavilion's gable
the roof: the mansard's faces, the dormers, the pavilion's gable, the corner pyramid and the great stack
the 21st Street flank's nearer half, the stoop's two flights and the iron fence
what_it_does_not_supply: the south flank, the rear and the 21st Street flank's far half

what_it_supplies: year built, architect, style and owners as the marker states them for 2009, 2100, 2115, 2126 and 2140 Prairie
the year each house was razed, as the marker gives it

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.
what_it_supplies: Footprints, lots and street widths from 20th to 22nd Street between Indiana and Calumet, as of 1911, at the copy's coarser resolution
The position of Twentieth Street, which is vacated between Indiana and Calumet today
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2351) in place by T-1919 (the S10A envelope package of the T-1837 programme) onto the K01 frontage kit, liberty L-k01-2100-sherman-1919: the plan and footprint off the 1911 sheet and the 1876 American Architect plate's 'Plan of First Story', the elevations off the c. 1890 photograph (two prints: Chicagology's and J. W. Taylor's at the Art Institute). The carving, the stone bands, the arched and pointed heads, the side flight of the stoop are T-1920's (the architecture and the image gate); T-3700 built the corner's oriel on its column, its gable and the pyramid behind it.
